# Test API compatibility with darwinkit's NSApplication
# This test compares the go doc output of our generated NSApplication
# with darwinkit's to ensure API compatibility
#
# CURRENT STATE: This test will FAIL until we implement proper class generation
# with Go struct types and methods (not just documentation comments)
#
# Goal: Generate code that matches darwinkit's API:
#   type Application struct { ... }
#   func Application_SharedApplication() Application
#   func (a_ Application) Run()
#   func (a_ Application) Terminate(sender objc.IObject)
#   etc.

env INPUT_DIR=$HOME/.appledocs/cache/developer.apple.com/tutorials/data/documentation

# Generate AppKit bindings with NSApplication
exec generate-framework-bindings -framework AppKit -input $INPUT_DIR -output api_test

# Check if classes.gen.go was generated
# Currently this file only contains documentation comments, not actual types
exists api_test/appkit/classes.gen.go

# Verify NSApplication is at least documented
grep 'NSApplication' api_test/appkit/classes.gen.go

# TODO: These checks will work once we implement proper class generation
# For now, just check that the file contains documentation

# Check the current output format (documentation only)
grep '// NSApplication : NSResponder' api_test/appkit/classes.gen.go

# What we NEED to generate (will fail until implemented):
# The following assertions check for actual Go type definitions and methods
# that match darwinkit's API. These will all fail currently.

# Check for the Application type struct
! grep 'type Application struct' api_test/appkit/classes.gen.go

# This test documents the gap: we generate documentation comments
# but not the actual Go types and methods needed for API compatibility
#
# To pass this test, we need to generate code like darwinkit:
#   1. Type definitions: type Application struct { Responder }
#   2. Constructor methods: func Application_SharedApplication() Application
#   3. Instance methods: func (a_ Application) Run()
#   4. Method wrappers for all NSApplication methods
#
# Expected method count from darwinkit: ~100+ methods on Application type
